subject: Hybrid VPC Gateway design review and control-plane/data-plane separation
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Hybrid VPC Gateway: initial architecture review request

Hi Markus / team,

Thanks for taking this on. We're evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment where our inference dataplane runs in our VPC (AWS us-west-2) and we want a lightweight control plane that Redwood manages but over private peering. Key asks:

- Clear control plane / data plane separation (no model weights ever leave our VPC)
- Minimal egress (need NAT/egress control and predictable IPs)
- Failover path if Redwood's control plane is unreachable
- A reference diagram and suggested firewall rules we can present to our networking team

Attached is a short doc with our network constraints and compliance requirement (acme-initial-network-requirements.docx). Can we get a design review and a clear list of ports/IPs for our security team?

We'd like to target a review meeting next week.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Director, Infrastructure
Acme AI

Jane — thanks for the details and the doc. Happy to run the review. Proposed next steps:

1) Internal prep: we’ll draft a reference diagram showing control-plane endpoints, recommended peering, and egress NAT placement.
2) Security checklist: ports, IP ranges, TLS/key management options, and a fallback plan.
3) Review meeting: 60-minute sync with your infra + our network engineer.

I attached a short proposal + an early reference diagram (redwood-hybrid-vpc-proposal.pdf) so your team can pre-check. Can you do Wed 18 Nov 10:00am PT? If not, propose a couple times.

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VPC Gateway: initial architecture review request

Hi Jane — looped in our infra lead Karthik and attached an annotated flow focused on control-plane authentication and the recommended data-plane isolation. High-level notes below and in the diagram: 

- Control plane: OAuth2 mTLS to a set of managed endpoints (we can publish static IPs or use customer-managed PrivateLink).
- Data plane: model serving nodes run in your VPC; data never leaves your VPC except optional telemetry via a push endpoint you control.
- Egress: recommend putting NAT + centralized proxy in a dedicated subnet; we list explicit ports: 443 outbound for control plane, 12345 for KV sync only if enabled.

Quick ask from our side: do you require HSM-backed key storage or is KMS (AWS) acceptable?

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VPC Gateway: initial architecture review request

Thanks Laura — diagram looks useful. A couple of clarifying questions before the meeting: 

1) Control-plane reachability — we need a model where we can either (A) allow a small set of Redwood-managed IPs via our firewall, or (B) use AWS PrivateLink/Transit Gateway for cross-account peering. Do you support both?
2) Data-plane egress — we have strict data residency and must prevent accidental outgoing connections. Does Redwood provide an image-level lockdown or egress ACLs?
3) Failure modes — if Redwood's control plane is temporarily unreachable, can the dataplane continue serving cached prefixes / rolling-forward using pinned model versions? How graceful is the degradation?

Also: we need an exported list of firewall rules your network team will ask for (IP ranges, ports, expected FQDNs).

Looking forward to Wed if the time holds.

Jane

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Follow-up: control-plane/data-plane details and failure modes

Jane — answering your numbered items from the last email and adding a recommended firewall diff your team can apply: 

1) Reachability options:
- Option A (Static IPs): Redwood can publish a small /28 range for control-plane endpoints for your egress whitelist. We maintain redundancy across AZs but the IP set is stable for a release window.
- Option B (PrivateLink): supported for Dedicated and Private customers; we can provision an endpoint service and share the service name for a one-time peering setup.

2) Data-plane egress controls:
- We provide a hardened runtime image and recommend deploying with host-level egress ACLs (security groups + NACLs) that only allow outbound to our control-plane IPs or to a pre-approved telemetry endpoint.
- We can ship a sample iptables/NACL config (see attachment: sample-firewall-rules.txt).

3) Failure modes and graceful degradation:
- Short network loss (<5m): dataplane continues serving from local KV/prefix cache for warm prompts and pinned model versions; control-plane requests are retried with exponential backoff.
- Extended loss (>5m): we surface a degraded state to the app (503s for new model pulls) but existing pinned endpoints continue to serve inference.
- Rollback/backfill: we support an operator-triggered local rollback to the last known-good model version if control-plane coordination is unavailable.

Attached: a cleaned-up diagram and a proposal PDF for your security team. Please review and tell us which reachability option you prefer so we can prepare PrivateLink details if needed.

Regards,
Markus

Markus / team — this is great, thank you. Acme prefers Option B (PrivateLink) for the initial rollout. Two quick follow-ups: 

- Can you produce the PrivateLink service name and a short runbook for our network ops (we need the service name, required IAM permissions, and expected latency/throughput targets)?
- For SOC2 auditors we will also need a short statement that model weights are never egressed from our VPC and a pointer to any audit logs you can provide for control-plane API calls.

If you can send the PrivateLink details and a 1-page SOC2-friendly note, we can move to procurement.

Best,
Jane
